newsitem.title: BURMA: Japanese company invests in pearl culture in Burma.
newsitem.headline: Japanese company invests in pearl culture in Burma.

text.p: Tasaki Shinju Co Ltd will invest $50 million to cultivate pearls in Burma on a production-sharing basis, a government official said on Friday.
An official from the Ministry of Mines' Myanma Pearl Enterprises told Reuters Tasaki Shinju signed a 15-year contract to cultivate pearls in the Myeik archipelago.
It is the second foreign investment in pearl production in Burma, the official said.
The ministry will sell 97 pearl lots worth $1.94 million through competitive bidding and 74 other lots by tender at an auction on March 8.
